answer.rationale: With the line at 94% of committed volume and no buffer, any delivery risk is amplified; memory_c2 shows the low-cost vendor missed SLA in 3 of 4 quarters, making a primary-vendor switch too risky right now despite the cost mandate. Memory_c4 shows that benchmarking and renegotiating at renewal previously recovered real margin and improved payment terms without disrupting supply, and memory_c1/c6 confirm incumbent renewals (especially multi-year) preserve integration stability and can still cut unit cost via volume pricing. Given the 14-day expiration deadline and the finance-mandated 18% cut, the single decision this cycle should be to negotiate aggressively with the incumbent at renewal—pursuing benchmarked pricing and possibly a multi-year term—rather than switching vendors or deferring, since deferral risks a lapse with no buffer and switching risks known SLA failures. I verified c4 (negotiation outcome) and c2 (switch-vendor risk) since they most directly bear on the risk/cost tradeoff for this decision.
